title: Honest Review for Poppy AI (With a Detailed Setup Video)
comment:
As a content creator juggling multiple YouTube channels and constantly looking for ways to save time, I gave Poppy AI a try after seeing it pop up with a compelling lifetime deal on AppSumo. I’ve been using it for over a month, and here’s my honest experience:

If you want a hands-on walkthrough and an honest look at real results, I highly recommend watching the Saas Guru video review:
👉 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UpsoNzJODNQ (YouTube Link)
It covers practical use cases, live demos, tips, and a direct comparison with other popular AI tools.

👍 What’s Great:

True Time Saver for Content Creation:
The workspace is incredibly intuitive—Poppy AI guides you step-by-step, whether you’re brainstorming, scripting YouTube videos, or repurposing old content into fresh blog posts. Instead of spending hours switching between notes, planners, and scripts, everything is centralized and visually organized.

Flexible & Visual Workflows:
The drag-and-drop “thought board” is a killer feature. I love mapping out video ideas, batch planning titles, and even collaborating with my small team. It feels way more organized than a Google Doc or linear AI chat.

Brand Voice Training:
I was pleasantly surprised by how well Poppy AI adapts to unique brand tones. Uploading sample content helped create scripts that actually sound like me, not just ChatGPT with generic responses.

Content Repurposing Magic:
Taking a YouTube script and spinning it into blog and social snippets is genuinely just a few clicks. The AI keeps context from the main topic, so there’s less editing after the fact. Huge productivity boost!

Support & Active Development:
The founder and team are responsive on AppSumo and in the built-in chat. Bugs and feature requests actually get noticed and worked on, which gives me confidence for the future.

👎 What Needs Work:

Learning Curve & Occasional Bugs:
At first, the visual workflow felt a little overwhelming coming from list-based AI tools. There were also minor glitches like stuck drag-and-drops and UI refreshes, but nothing that stopped my projects.

AI Credit Limitations:
Depending on your deal tier, Poppy AI works on a credit system similar to other GPT-powered tools. If you create lots of long-form content or multiple projects per week, you’ll burn through those credits faster than expected.

Occasional Output Quality Fluctuations:
While most scripts are solid, sometimes the AI outputs need a bit of rework to match my channel’s storytelling style exactly. Not a dealbreaker, but not always perfect.

Still Developing Features:
While the workspace is amazing, I’d love to see deeper integrations (like direct YouTube or WordPress publishing) and further automation for social media. I know they’re on the roadmap.

Overall:
Poppy AI really does what it promises—speeding up ideation, planning, and content creation for YouTubers and content marketers. It’s replaced three or four tools for me, and lets me focus on the creative, not tech headaches. The current lifetime deal is a no-brainer if you value time and want a genuinely visual AI workspace.

title: Useful concept, but the real cost is hidden behind expensive credits
comment:
BUB? ref: 4) You mentioned that the upselling feels too aggressive and to be completely honest with you, what happened in your account was A BUG 🐞.You called me five times 5 minutes after I registered my phone number I was forced to add in the signup!!!

Poppy has an interesting visual workflow and the ability to organise research, videos, PDFs, and content ideas on a board is useful. The core concept has potential.

However, the pricing structure seriously weakens the value of the AppSumo lifetime deal.

After purchasing, I discovered that API access is not included in the AppSumo tiers. It requires an additional Power User subscription. This matters because connecting Poppy with other AI tools, agents, and automation workflows was one of my main intended use cases.

The credit pricing is also excessive:

3,000 credits cost $150
6,000 credits cost $210
10,000 credits cost $350

These are one-time purchases, not recurring credits. Yet the upgrade page calls this an “AppSumo Lifetime Credits Deal” and refers to “lifetime credit boosts.” That wording is confusing because the credits are only added once.

The practical cost can therefore include the original lifetime deal, expensive one-time credit packages, and another recurring subscription for API access. That is very different from the value I expected from a lifetime purchase.

The upselling also feels too aggressive. I was encouraged to upgrade with messaging such as “You’re on Fire” and “Go Viral with Poppy AI” while my account still showed 0 of 1,000 credits used. That creates pressure before the product has even been properly evaluated.

Poppy may be useful for some creators, but buyers should understand the full cost structure before purchasing. For my intended workflow, the missing API access, expensive credits, unclear “lifetime” wording, and aggressive upselling make the deal poor value.

title: If you have the money - buy tier6, NOW!
comment:
One word: AWESOME! 🌮​🌮​🌮​🌮​🌮​🌮​🌮​🌮​🌮​🌮​

I've been using Poppy AI for a while on a lower tier from their website and upgraded to Tier 6 after seeing it land on AppSumo — and the chatbot & API feature was the deciding factor.

My use case is different from most reviewers here: I'm an (agile) consultant working with German midsize companies, not an "only one" content creator. But I'll use it for some other use cases in the feature, too.

Honesty first: on a pure ROI basis, Poppy doesn't replace my existing stack. I already run Straico (AppSumo LTD Deal :) for LLM access and n8n for automation — so the API and content generation features largely overlap with what I have. If you're already running a self-hosted automation infrastructure, be aware of this before buying.

What keeps me here — and what pushed me to Tier 6 — is two things. First, the visual board. There's something genuinely different about seeing your knowledge sources, connections, and outputs laid out spatially. It changes how I think about a project, not just how fast I execute it. That's hard to replicate in a workflow tool. It's how I can structure and see data!

Second, the chatbot & API. Giving people a dedicated AI assistant trained on the specific project knowledge base (in an easy Poppy.ai-way) I build for my online courses is a real differentiator. No Poppy account needed on their end, just a link. I'm still testing credit consumption for this use case, but the ability to choose a lighter model for Q&A helps keep usage efficient. My test (4 websites and one text field with general instructions):

13,151 -> 13,128 (Sonnet 4.6)
13,128 -> 13,099 (Sonnet 4.6)
13,099 -> 13,098 (gpt4-mini)

... looks easy 🤌​🤩​

I asked some general questions and as you can see the consumptions (in my not complex case) is nothing. It's very low level even I know, it can go up. But then simply ask the team - I think they will help to rebuild and give tips.

I also want to be transparent about why I bought at Tier 6 despite the overlap with my stack: I want to support this team. I was in an onboarding call some time ago (for my old LTD). They even send you bonus credits for just be in there. They look carefully on what you want to build and give you feedback. No selling, no pushing - this is caring! They want YOU to be successful.

They've built something genuinely good, they're bootstrapped, and they've priced this sustainably instead of racing to the bottom and then killing the LTD six months later — which I've seen happen too many times on AppSumo (looking at you, Adilo BigCommand). That kind of integrity is worth something. Don't disappoint me, please :) This is my highest invest 🫰​ I always did on AppSumo. But it feels good.

The team is responsive and honest. I asked a detailed question about credit usage for client-facing chatbots and got a straight answer — no overpromising, just clear explanation of the variables and levers to optimize. And I tested it after buying in details (see above). If I ever wanted to work again with or for a company - Poppy would be the choice ❤️

One thing I'm watching: the roadmap mention of monthly credit limits per chatbot. If that lands, this becomes a very clean B2B product, not just a creator tool. And some GDPR features like DPAs and so on. And if you bring MCP to the tiers (or some higher ones) you will made my day.

For consultants, coaches, or anyone building client-facing knowledge products: worth serious consideration. Just be honest with yourself about your existing stack first.

Downsides (hard to mention anything)
- Privacy and GDPR are the most important things here - I don't use my customer data within the app. That's something I only do on local LLMs on my own machines. But hence I does not use it with customer data directly, not an issue for me. But for all EU & German Companies there might be some open questions.
- The ChatBot needs to be CNAME covered to bring real value (for me). In my current setup it's also not much relevant.

Guys - thank you so much to be here and give us this change of being part of your fantastic product. If you need something we (at least I) can do for you, just drop a line!

Sebastian

title: The Cure for AI Chat Fatigue: Sort of a Visual Revolution
comment:
Artificial intelligence is everywhere now. It’s like we’ve all got these ghosts in the machine, and everybody is sitting around talking to screens. But those standard chat boxes? They are traps.

You try to build something big, something with a lot of moving parts, and suddenly you’re just a glorified secretary, copying and pasting and losing your mind trying to remember what the machine said five minutes ago.

You end up burning through your tokens (your digital money) just forcing the robot to remember the past. It's a waste of time and cash. But then I tested Poppy AI, and it fixed the two biggest headaches of this whole robot-talking business.

First, it gives you a visual board, which is basically a real, wide-open map. You can see every word you put in and every word it spit back out, all laid out like a big, complicated family tree.

Second, you can actually unplug things when you're done with them. You just look at a node, decide it's useless history, and disconnect it with a click. This means you stop paying the machine to remember things you've already moved past.

These visual boards change the way you work, letting you lay out these long, complicated ideas and actually see them making sense. You move faster, and you can change directions when the wind blows without losing your entire map.

Here’s a little secret from the trenches: it works remarkably well with Claude Desktop. I won't bore you with the deep nerd details today, but if you want to stretch your digital dollars, making those two talk to each other is exactly how you do it.

And Poppy isn’t just a drawing board, either. This thing can dig through the absolute noise of social media and find the actual gold, pulling up the viral posts and the ads that are actually winning. If you know what you’re looking for in your own little corner of the marketing world, those research tools are worth a whole lot of real-world cash.

I sat down for an onboarding session with Charan, and he didn't just read a corporate script to me. He showed me his own process, opened up the hood of his business, and helped me figure out how to make this tool work for my own specific situation.

The proof is in the work itself. Just this week, sitting at my desk, I've mapped out three entire, deep-dive marketing plans for niches. I built the opt-in forms, the freebies to get people in the door, the welcome emails—the whole complicated dance of getting people to listen.

Now, all I have to do is write the mix of short and long-form content that sounds like me. Except I don't. I just have to coach Poppy through some best practices to get there.

So here's the truth of it. If you've been carrying around half-cooked plans in your head for years, just letting them rattle around in the dark, you need to see them out in the light. Poppy AI gives you that light and the traction you need to finally make them real.

title: A strong tool for visual, non-linear AI workflows
comment:
I originally found Poppy months ago and had been watching it because the monthly subscription felt outside my budget. When the AppSumo deal came up, it felt like a no-brainer.

After using it and having an onboarding call with Christian Santos, I can say Poppy is not just “another AI tool” in the usual chatbot sense. Yes, it is still an AI tool, but the real value is the visual, non-linear workspace. For people who collect a lot of inspiration, work with videos, build frameworks, or think in connected layers instead of straight lines, Poppy makes a lot of sense.

My favorite use case so far is being able to add videos to a board, pull out the frameworks, keep the original videos there for later reference, and then use multiple chats on the board to mix and match context. That is much easier than trying to remember which Gemini or ChatGPT thread had “that one video” or re-uploading the same reference because I cannot remember the exact thumbnail.

The “notes for AI” feature is also a standout. I can tell Poppy exactly what part of a video I want it to mimic, extract, or use for a specific case. That makes the video more useful as directed context instead of just dumping a transcript into an AI tool and hoping it figures out what matters.

The onboarding call was excellent. Christian looked at what I was already figuring out, then expanded on it with practical tips around credit usage, focused chats, extracting frameworks, keeping assets on the board, and using context more intentionally. It did not feel canned. It felt like he actually understood how I was trying to use the software.

I also appreciate the templates, prompts, and community resources. Not because prompts are the end-all be-all, but because each AI system has its own way it wants to be spoken to. Seeing how people successfully use Poppy helps you learn the language of the tool faster.

The strongest result I have gotten so far was a set of carousels that came out beautiful and followed my design guide closely. That matters to me because I do not just want generic AI output. I need the tool to understand and preserve my creative direction.

My caveats: mobile support needs to improve, and I would love stronger TikTok/Instagram discovery by tag, niche, or adjacent content. Credit usage can also go quickly if you do not understand how context groups work, so I think Poppy would benefit from a dedicated best-practices class on token/credit usage. I would also like clearer API documentation and more education on using Poppy alongside agents or external AI tools.

Overall, I would recommend Poppy most to visual thinkers, neurodivergent or non-linear thinkers, content creators, educators, coaches, and AI power users who need a better way to organize inspiration, extract frameworks, and turn scattered context into usable outputs.

It has room to improve, but the core idea is strong. Poppy gives you a way to see and reuse your thinking instead of losing it inside endless chat threads.

title: One of the best AppSumo Offerings
comment:
Poppy AI is one of the more expensive AppSumo offerings, with an entry price of nearly $250, though members can sometimes access a discount. It is primarily aimed at content creators and allows users to gather information from multiple sources, including documents, videos, web pages, and even links to other applications. Poppy then turns that material into a knowledge base you can converse with, similar in some ways to NotebookLM or Zemith.

I originally bought Poppy AI for one reason: proposal writing. To do that well, I needed a way to organize company information, product details, prior proposals, customer requirements, and government proposal guidance in one place. When I purchased my license, AppSumo was offering a limited-time discount, and I chose to upgrade, making it a significant investment.

Before I even got started, Poppy impressed me with its support and onboarding. I was invited to a one-on-one 30-minute call, followed by a series of five live-streamed training sessions the next week. I couldn’t attend live, but I was given access to the recordings. The week after that, I received another notice about a session introducing new features. Poppy is easily one of the most engaged companies I’ve encountered.

The platform itself is straightforward: load in your sources and start asking questions. It works very well. That said, I quickly noticed that my tier two subscription was burning through credits. Part of that was because I was using a more expensive model. Another factor was the size of my knowledge base. With so many sources, Poppy had to process a lot of information every time I asked a question.

To reduce token usage, I downgraded to a smaller model and started using GPT-5.4 Mini, which still performs very well. I also asked Poppy to create a single, densely packed Markdown document containing the key information. I copied that into a Word document, saved it, disconnected the other sources, and worked from the Markdown alone. The results were still strong, but token usage dropped significantly.

I’m still a beginner with Poppy AI and only scratching the surface of what it can do. Even so, I would say it is one of the most valuable products I have purchased. The quality of the output is better than anything I’ve been able to get before.

title: Great concept, but the credit system FOR THE SAME PDF needs urgent improvement
comment:
Great concept
Poppy AI has a lot of things I genuinely like. The visual board approach is very useful, especially when working with different sources and trying to organize research, ideas, documents, videos, and content in one place. The overall concept is excellent for content creation, research, marketing, educational material, and building workflows around source material.

One area, however, seriously weakens the experience: the way credits are consumed when working with attached documents.

When a PDF remains connected to a chat, its content is processed again with every new AI message. THIS MEANS THAT A LONG DOCUMENT CAN REPEATEDLY CONTRIBUTE TO CREDIT CONSUMPTION EVEN WHEN THE SOURCE ITSELF HAS NOT CHANGED.

For users who work with large PDFs, manuals, educational material, research papers, transcripts, or other long-form resources, this can make credits disappear surprisingly quickly. A workflow that naturally requires several follow-up questions can become much more expensive than expected simply because the same source content is being processed repeatedly.

This is not just a small pricing detail. It directly affects how freely and effectively the platform can be used for serious research and content workflows.

Poppy would be significantly stronger IF UPLOADED DOCUMENTS COULD BE INDEXED ONCE and then referenced more efficiently in subsequent questions, RATHER THAN REPEATEDLY CONSUMING CREDITS for the SAME UNCHANGED MATERIAL.

The product itself has a very strong concept and a lot of potential, and the visual workflow is one of its biggest strengths. But the current document-related credit consumption is an important weakness that should be improved, because it can make otherwise normal usage unnecessarily expensive.
